[i]If I could describe hell in any way, shape, or form it would be Bombardo, on that accursed day I witnessed the damnation of the righteous and unrighteous, but it wasn't done by a divine force. It was him, a man so evil rumours around my home village he sold his soul to the devil for power. He never fell short of these tales, he was like an alien wearing human skin. There was no emotion in that man's soul, no empathy for the suffering he inflicted on others, hell - I'd bet if he even tried to repent for his sins that GOD would reject him. 

What he had done on that day to me, my family, and those I love I cannot forgive, nor can I forget.  I can never forget the sight of flesh being pulverised by bullets, the echoes of screams from the blood cloud above, the rolling of tanks over those who were crippled. All of it, it was too much for me. But what I can do now is tell what I know.
[b]_______________________[/b]

I woke to the sound of gunfire, the same gunfire that deafened me. 

My lungs burned. Dust filled my throat. Something heavy pinned my leg, I wanted to move it but I couldn't. I had no strength in me, all I felt was the immense pain. Gunpowder blanketed my eyes, I could not see. I tried thrashing around wiggling my body back and forth, but I just couldn't free myself. Then I looked up, and I was greeted by the horrible sight of mangled flesh, broken bones, and a horde of flies. I couldn't process the sight before me, hundreds of bodies littered the city block around me, I kept shifting my glance across the block until my eyes locked with something familiar. The mauled woman in front of me was my decapitated mother. "Mother...?" I groaned with all the remaining strength I had, I couldn't comprehend the situation I was in. I wanted to scream. But then, I heard a group of men approaching from my left. These men couldn't be civilians, they would've been shot already. Then, the second best guess came to my mind. I immediately swallowed my cries and limped my body as if I was a lifeless corpse. A few moments later, the approaching men finally reached me and looked at my body before continuing, I heard the screams of a woman echo before a loud gunshot interrupted it. I was right, these men were not coming to save us, they were the bastards who did it. The incapable disgraces of human beings that turned my world upside down. I wanted to lash out and attack one of them, but deep down I knew my effort would be futile.  

After what felt like years, the men finished their search and began picking up the bodies and dumping them into trucks. I felt a sharp pain erupting in my throat, the smoke that had filled my lungs multiplied this feeling by tenfold. I needed to cough. But I couldn't, if I did I'd be as good as dead. Then I felt a cold hand touch my back, I stood as still as I possibly could. My mind was racing, this is where I could die. Two men lifted me up, I felt an excruciating pain from my leg, they ripped my body out of the pile of bodies and then lifted me onto the truck. I cried in silence, for I could only feel anguish. 

Around 15 minutes later and I finally regained awareness, I looked around my surroundings analyzing where I was. From what I could infer, I was on a truck. My leg was severely wounded, mangled to an unrecognizable state. But if I didnt do anything, where they were taking me wouldve probably been a worse fate than city block. As I shifted my gaze all around the bed of the truck I saw an opening. A chance for me to escape. A pile of bodies was lined up in a manner that would allow me to crawl into and then out of the truck with minimal effort or making a scene. With all the remaining strength I had, I thrashed both of my hands in a forward motion. With each inch I covered I felt the pain increase tenfold, but I had to keep going. When I finally reached the pile I lifted my upper body above the carcasses and pushed my head so I could get a view of the road and see how fast the truck was going.

Signs passed like blurs, I felt a haunting chill down my spine, I couldnt. But I must, Im all that I have left. And Im all my family has left. I must. In a final valiant act of effort, I lifted my body above the cargo bed, and thrusted myself into the active road. I hit my face first, the impact blinded me for a couple seconds, when I lifted my hand to touch my mouth I noticed I was missing some teeth. But the pain was so immense that it had all gone numb. I couldnt feel my body anymore. My body tumbled across the road like a tumbleweed, I spinned more times than I could count. When I finally gained full consciousness I pushed on, dragging my mangled body into the nearby forest where I found a ditch that I could hide in for the coming hours. 

But the nightmare hadnt ended yet, it had only begun.
